articles.title: Una actuación para recordar: “Alonso es el maestro del caos”
articles.standfirst: El asturiano logra su mejor resultado del curso... y sus rivales reconocen el valor de lo logrado en Sepang
articles.summary: El asturiano logra su mejor resultado del curso... y sus rivales reconocen el valor de lo logrado en Sepang
articles.body: Una conversación de radio tras la finalización del Gran Premio de Bahréin en Sepang hizo un resumen a la perfección de lo que había ocurrido en la pista. “Lo has escuchado bien, sí. Alonso es P8”, contaba el ingeniero de Oscar Piastri a su piloto al recitar la clasificación. Y el de McLaren lanzó una respuesta sencilla: “Siempre, es el maestro del caos”. En el equipo papaya habían vivido en sus carnes como el veterano asturiano aguantaba el tipo y dejaba a Norris detrás. Con el mayor botín de puntos tras un año gris en lo mecánico. Alonso encontró más y más en un fin de semana en el que el Aston Martin ofrecía más garantías. En Sepang hay dos rectas importantes y el AMR26 rondaba en el déficit de los 20 km/h, pero en las zonas de chasis y de piloto cambió la cosa. Sin una actualización importante desde la de Hungría y Holanda, pero cambiando el paso con el desgaste de los neumáticos y un Alonso brutal en la lectura de carrera. “Había pilotos, como Hülkenberg con Norris, que se metieron en líos y se quedaron sin batería en dos vueltas. Yo la guardaba para las rectas y la tenía a tope”, explicó. Esa gestión pudo dar más premio todavía. Pero faltó un golpe más, quizá de fortuna, a su favor. Por ejemplo, el motor Honda no vivió el apagón por el software que otros propulsores, el de Ferrari especialmente, sí. Pero la carrera se paró. “Estaba Hamilton parado y se estresaron”, apuntó el propio Alonso. Y después en las condiciones mixtas navegó como podía con las gomas de seco. De hecho, iba más rápido que su histórico rival y le llegó a adelantar al tirarle el coche. Pero no se secó por completo y el coche de seguridad fue lo que le devolvió a la batalla. “Me sentía bien, pasé a Hamilton… pero no era la decisión correcta. Iba muy lento con las gomas lisas”, explicó ante Sky. Pero en ese momento se acabaron los errores y Aston y Alonso clavaron el plan. Avanzando en carrera, pasando a Ocon y Lindblad en dos manos a manos y sabiendo cuándo montar el último juego para el final de carrera. “Habrá pocos fines de semana así y no puedes cometer errores”, deslizó. Lo mejor es que viene otro trazado favorable, las calles de Singapur. Con el componente adicional de ser en formato sprint con lo que habrá muy poco tiempo para dejar al coche ajustado al gusto del piloto en el circuito. “Soy optimista, absolutamente. Es una pista mejor para nuestras características que Malasia. El rendimiento de este fin de semana es alentador para buscar repetir… o mejorar”, avanzó el bicampeón. Una declaración de intenciones. “Tengo ganas, serán cinco días de espera emocionantes hasta la clasificación”, cerró. El mejor Alonso ha vuelto. Con la renovación bajo el brazo y una oportunidad de aumentar una cuenta de puntos que ya tiene siete unidades tras el buen 8° del Gran Premio de Bahréin.

articles.summary: Tras el "show" de Sepang, llegamos a Marina Bay
articles.body: Último Gran Premio del triplete y el Mundial de F1 se va a Singapur. Tras haber regresado a Malasia, al sustituir a Bahréin en el circuito de Sepang, casi 10 años después, el campeonato vuelve a recuperar un poco de normalidad y aterriza en Marina Bay, Singapur. Eso sí, hay Sprint. Una carrera loca, por no decir la que más en lo que llevamos de temporada, tras haberse visto diversos sucesos extraños que ponen en entredicho la nueva reglamentación de la Fórmula 1 y que sin lugar a duda tendrá que ser exhaustivamente revisada. Max Verstappen volvió a llevarse la Pole y a ganar, tras casi una temporada sin hacerlo. El de Red Bull fue el más listo de la clase y tras casi dos horas de carrera, sumado a numerosos incidentes, el neerlandés se llevó la victoria por encima de Kimi Anotnelli y Lewis Hamilton. A Antonelli le salen bien las cosas. El de Mercedes parecía haber perdido un poco de ese brillo que ha tenido durante toda la temporada, llegando incluso Russell a empezar a recortarle y pensar en el Mundial. Sin embargo, cuando parecía que podría recuperar un poco de lo que perdió las últimas dos carreras, un fallo en la Unidad de Potencia del piloto británico, hizo que éste sumara otro cero y Antonelli le metiera 18 puntos más, aventajándole en 84 y poniendo muy a tiro el Mundial. Un 8º puesto fue lo que firmó Fernando Alonso en Sepang. El asturiano ya sabía lo que era ganar aquí y era, de hecho, el piloto de la actual parrilla con más victorias en este circuito. Clasificó 12º y nos hizo soñar con los puntos, a pesar de que el Aston Martin no nos permita siquiera pensarlo. Aún y así, Alonso pudo aprovecharse del lío y sacarle el máximo partido a la situación, consiguiendo dos puntos que le saben a gloria. Mientras, Sainz se llevó la cruz de la moneda. El madrileño, a pesar de las mejoras implantadas en su Williams en Bakú, sufrió más de la cuenta. Tan sólo pudo clasificar 13º y, un toque con Bortoleto al inicio de la carrera, sentenciaron por completo cualquier mínima posibilidad que pudiera tener el de Williams, finalizando la carrera 17º. Como es habitual, el Gran Premio de Singapur de Fórmula 1 2026 se podrá ver en directo por televisión a través de DAZN F1 y en Movistar +. También tienes la opción de seguir todo lo que suceda en la carrera en el circuito de Sepang a través de los directos de MARCA.com y la transmisión de la carrera en Radio MARCA. articles.title: F1 Sprint: Schedule, points, results format explained, qualifying, race and venues for 2026 season
articles.summary: A look at how the Sprint weekend works ahead of its final appearance in 2026 at the Singapore Grand Prix this weekend; watch every session starting this Friday with Practice at 9.30am and Sprint Qualifying at 1.30pm, live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event
articles.body:
Six of F1's 24 race weekends again run to the Sprint format in the 2026 season:

October 9-11: Singapore Grand Prix, Singapore

Canada, the Netherlands and Singapore host Sprint weekends for the first time while the British Grand Prix returned as a Sprint round for the first time since 2021.

The Sprint format - with a short-form Saturday race as its centrepiece - was added to the F1 schedule at select events from the 2021 season in a bid to further spice up the action on tracks known to be good for overtaking, while also ensuring competitive track sessions for fans attending the circuit and watching on TV on all three days of the race weekend.

Initially introduced at just three venues per season before growing to six from 2023, such weekends feature a rejigged schedule, with the Sprint having its own qualifying session on Friday before a 100km race on Saturday , in which crucial extra world championship points are on offer.

Sprint weekends begin with a single free practice session on Friday, which as usual lasts for one hour.

Sprint Qualifying then follows later on Friday.

Saturday then opens with the 100km Sprint contest, followed by Grand Prix Qualifying later in the day to set the grid for the Grand Prix itself on Sunday.

The Friday session to set the Sprint grid will follow the same format as last season, with each of its three parts running to the same knockout rules as full Qualifying but to shorter durations to address engine and tyre concerns.

The initial aim is that each car only has one flying lap in each session, although two runs can be completed in SQ1 while SQ2 and SQ3 do allow time for two timed laps without a pit stop in between attempts.

The other significant difference between Sprint Qualifying and full Qualifying are restrictions on tyre usage in the former.

While drivers are free to use any of their available tyres in regular qualifying, in Sprint Qualifying they are only allowed to run one set of tyres in each part.

A new set of medium tyres is mandatory in SQ1 and SQ2, while a set of soft tyres - new or otherwise - is mandatory in SQ3.

What is the points system for the Sprint?

Points for the Sprint in 2026 remain unchanged.

A total of 36 points are on offer for the top eight finishers in Saturday's race. This is allocated as follows:

Pit stops are few and far between given how short a Sprint is.

Unlike the Grand Prix, there is no mandatory change of tyres required and, unless cars suffer damage or puncture or it rains, don't expect them to leave the action on track for the pit lane between lights out and the chequered flag.

Drivers are free to run on whatever tyre compound - hard, medium or soft - that they wish.

How often can teams change their cars between sessions?

Since the current Sprint format was introduced, teams have had a second opportunity to make setup changes to their cars during the weekend.

The cars enter parc ferme when the first competitive session - Friday's Sprint Qualifying - gets under way. However, those restrictions are lifted after Saturday's Sprint, giving teams the opportunity to make further changes based on what they have learned from the opening sessions.

Teams can then use that information to fine-tune their setups ahead of full Qualifying. Once Qualifying begins, the cars are locked into parc ferme conditions again, with those setups carrying through to Sunday's Grand Prix.

articles.body:
2.25 Yarmouth - Legacy Link's sister Zhuri takes on Never An Angel

Legacy Link's full-sister Zhuri takes on debutant Never An Angel for Ed Walker who cost 460,000gns as a yearling.

The well-related filly Zhuri comes here for her second racecourse start, this time dropping to seven-furlongs after shaping well without seeing out the trip, dropping back in distance looks to suit her.

Ed Walker is 15 per cent with his two-year-olds this year and comes here with the 460,000gns No Nay Never-filly Never An Angel , with Kieran Shoemark taking the ride.

Baaeed has made a bright start to his stallion career and is represented here by the William Haggas-trained filly Faithful who is from a good family, being a half-sister to Italy for Aidan O'Brien and Bowmark, who shares the same connections.

Another beautifully bred runner, Lady Jemima is the most experienced in the field, with three starts to her name already, latterly producing an encouraging effort at Newmarket and she should progress again for the James Owen team.

8.30 Wolverhampton - Powder Monkey looks to complete a hat-trick

Powder Monkey looks to complete a hat-trick in the Race & Rest - Wolverhampton Holiday Inn Handicap , after wins at Wolverhampton and Lingfield.

He returned to the track after a break with a win at Lingfield Park in August, off a mark of 69. That victory pushed him up to 74 and he since went on to defy favouritism readily in the hands of Billy Loughnane. He is up to a mark of 78 today and the champion jockey-elect takes the ride again.

Dublin Bay won by seven lengths here back in May and was slapped with a ten-pound penalty for the effort. He has run with credit in deeper company on two starts since but will do well to overcome stall 12 off the same mark.

The top-weight Alfra Whiteburd landed a hat-trick at Pontefract in the summer for the Ivan Furtado team and hasn't lost much in defeat in two starts since but he returns to the All-Weather this evening and his four wins on this surface give him a chance.

4.05 Yarmouth - Box To Box and Cuff It take on eight rivals

Top-rated Box To Box and Cuff It will take on eight rivals in this competitive Haven Seashore Holiday Park Handicap .

Box To Box is without a win in his last five starts and is down to a mark of 87 but looked to have the race at his mercy last time at Chester, striking the front at the furlong pole before being run down close to home. Another bold show can be expected.

Cuff It is the most unexposed in here, just four career starts to his name. He had his handicap debut last time out at York in a competitive class two contest but found that company too hot. Back in a class four event today, he could run well.

Lucky Hero is in-form, having won two of his last three runs, his hat-trick bid was thwarted last time out as he was beaten a short margin into third after winning at Newmarket. Another big effort can't be dismissed.

1.50 Yarmouth - Awwjaan who is Irish 1000 Guineas-entered returns.

3.35 Yarmouth - Wootton Bassett-filly Endless Quest begins her career.

articles.title: Max Verstappen: Why Red Bull driver's victory at Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia was so special
articles.summary: Max Verstappen kept his streak of winning in every season since he joined Red Bull back in 2016 alive; after a difficult first half of the year, Red Bull have been on an upward trend so how important was his win on Sunday?
articles.body:
Verstappen was at his imperious best as he mastered the mixed conditions and Safety Car restarts to beat championship leader Kimi Antonelli and maintain his streak of winning at least one race every season since joining Red Bull in 2016.

Only two months ago, Verstappen's future was in the spotlight but he signed a new Red Bull contract during the summer break to stay with the team until at least the end of 2030, and Malaysia highlighted why the Dutchman had so much faith in the Milton Keynes squad.

How have Red Bull suddenly turned things around?

Having come within two points of becoming a five-time world champion last year, it became clear Verstappen would be unable to challenge for the title this season for the first time since 2020.

Red Bull, in collaboration with Ford, built their own power unit but it was actually the chassis which was a major weak point at the start of the season. In fact, the Red Bull-Ford engine was deemed to be the benchmark on the grid by the FIA after the first ADUO (Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities) review.

Verstappen has the ability to drive and get the most out of any racing car but even he struggled to have confidence in the unpredictable handling of the RB22 as he claimed just one podium in the opening seven races.

Red Bull brought a major upgrade package to June's Austrian Grand Prix which got rid of the car's excess weight and changed the aerodynamics.

It had an immediate effect as Verstappen finished less than two seconds behind race-winner George Russell on his way to second, was on course for third a week later at Silverstone until his rear wing failed, and took two more podiums before the summer break in Belgium and Hungary.

A rare mistake at his home race in Zandvoort saw Verstappen crash out on the opening lap but he was back on the podium in Monza and Madrid.

Red Bull brought more upgrades to Baku where Verstappen finished just two tenths behind Russell in Azerbaijan in F1's closest finish since 2002.

Outside of his crashes at the British and Dutch Grands Prix, Verstappen has been on the podium in the other seven races since the Austria upgrades. In some ways, his dominant weekend in Malaysia should not be a surprise because Red Bull have been on an upward trajectory.

"We had a very complicated and tough start to the year with all sorts of problems and just not being competitive enough," said Verstappen.

"But throughout the year, the team has been working very hard to understand our issues and bring good performance upgrades to the car and make it more driveable. Step by step, we've been getting closer and closer, and Sunday, and of course especially this whole weekend, we've been really in good form, so it's amazing.

"Very enjoyable to win here and also have our first victory for our own engine. It's an incredible project with a lot of partners and a lot of people that are dedicated to be where we are now, so a fantastic feeling."

Much credit must go to former team principal Christian Horner for the success of Red Bull-Ford powertrains, the venture he set up that has delivered far above expectations during its first campaign as an engine manufacturer.

However, Red Bull was somewhat in turmoil during Horner's final years at the team due to a power struggle following the death of co-founder Dietrich Mateschitz in 2022.

Several key members left the team including legendary F1 designer Adrian Newey, chief engineering officer Rob Marshall, sporting director Jonathan Wheatley, advisor Helmut Marko - and eventually Horner himself.

With it came question marks about Verstappen's own future at the team in 2024 and 2025, particularly when his father Jos Verstappen fell out with Horner.

Laurent Mekies replaced Horner as team principal in July 2025 and the Verstappen camp appears to have a far more harmonious relationship with the Frenchman, with Max especially appreciating Mekies' engineering background.

Twelve months ago, Red Bull suddenly found plenty of performance that saw Verstappen claim eight consecutive podiums, including four wins, to unexpectedly push Lando Norris close to the title.

How much of that was down to Mekies is hard to judge, given how quickly that step was made, but the development this year can certainly be put down to his leadership.

Mekies said following Verstappen's win on Sunday: "The credit goes to all the people involved who have been working incredibly hard on this project over the past five years. Everyone in Milton Keynes and at the track deserves this moment and should celebrate it as an important step towards many more victories in the future.

"This result confirms the progress we have been making in recent months. We were already close several times, and today we converted that pace. The team has been working tirelessly to improve our package, and weekends like this are the reward for that effort."

It's far too early to say Verstappen has definitely made the right decision by committing his future to Red Bull, and this can only be truly answered in 2027.

However, it has become clear the combination of Mekies as team principal, trust in technical director Pierre Wache and chief performance engineer Ben Waterhouse - both of whom have been with Red Bull for over a decade - are key parts of the puzzle to effectively rebuild a new Red Bull era around Verstappen.

"Everyone is contributing a lot and always trying to find performance, upgrades and push the team forward," Verstappen told Sky Sports F1 .

"In Baku we were quick in the corners but not on the straights compared to Mercedes. In Malaysia, we were decent in the corners and quick on the straights.

"Sometimes we just need to understand the whole package - why we are quick, why we were not so quick and take it step by step."

Red Bull have a history of developing their cars strongly and appear to be exhibiting that once more this season, so there's no reason to think Verstappen won't add to his 72 career wins during the seven remaining rounds.

Malaysia was just another reminder that the Red Bull-Verstappen combination is still an almighty force that was never likely to sleep for long, and may now be wide awake once more.

articles.title: NASCAR star rips sport for being slow and soft, another makes a shocking comeback & scorned wife bites back
articles.summary: Tony Stewart calls NASCAR Cup Series "neutered" in a viral rant, while Jennifer Jo Cobb owes $850,000 after a civil court affair accusation.
articles.body: Monday Morning Pit-Stop is a weekly NASCAR column that runs on OutKick.com and Fox News Digital. If you're looking for a normal NASCAR recap, go check out insufferable ESPN ... assuming they still know NASCAR exists. Five races down, five to go in the NASCAR Cup Series postseason. That's right. Feels like we just started these playoffs, and now this new version of The Chase is nearing the finish line. Serious question ... How do we feel about it? This is the first year NASCAR hasn't had it's usual win-and-advance format in over a decade, and I'm genuinely curious how everyone feels. NASCAR RACE INCLUDES HALF THE FIELD WRECKING, FURIOUS DRIVERS & HOLLYWOOD ACTOR RIPPING A 'LEFTIST, WOKE' MOVE Have you watched more? Less? The same? Do these races have the same fire they used to when every third race was an elimination race? Has it made any difference at all for you? I'll be honest ... I miss the old format. I do. I knew I would. Chase Briscoe won yesterday at Las Vegas. Kyle Larson and Tyler Reddick crossed the line while wrecking after Larson hit the wall trying to chase down Briscoe on the final turn. It was a decent race, and a fun finish ... but I just feel like it's lost some juice. The stakes don't feel quite as high to me. I still enjoy it, but these playoffs — or Chase, whatever NASCAR wants us to call them — have just felt sort of neutered. And yes, I stole that word from Tony Stewart, who is currently viral right now for some eyebrow-raising comments he made about NASCAR earlier this year. You'll see. RISING NASCAR STAR JUMPED, ATTACKED & BEATEN AT AMERICA'S MOST FAMOUS HOT DOG SHACK What else? I've got Kasey Kahne, amazingly, coming out of retirement, a scorned wife going after a NASCAR driver after she seduced her husband (true story), and Brad Keselowski has been pushed out the door by his own team, which makes no sense given the team stunk before Brad got there and was actually respectable the past few years. Dummies. I'm not surprised, though, given his partners are associated with my Red Sox, and they're run just about as poorly as any professional sports team on the planet right now. Four tires, a splash of that Sunoco racin' fuel, and maybe a few more horses for Tony Stewart ... Monday Morning Pit-Stop — the 'NASCAR's Been Neutered' edition — is LIVE! Where there's Smoke ... Look, we're gonna break down yesterday's race at Vegas here in a bit. I promise. It was an OK race, with a decent finish that probably would've been a lot better if the cars weren't horrible. Take a look at Saturday's O'Reilly Series ending to see what I mean. But first, I do want to dive into these comments from Tony Stewart, which made the internet rounds over the weekend. Tony, who retired from full-time Cup racing in 2016, has never been known to mince words. I agree with a lot of his takes. I don't agree with others. For instance, he weirdly bashed fans and the media for mourning Kyle Busch earlier this year because he claimed we didn't care about Kyle Busch "the person" when he was alive. It was odd. So no, I don't always agree with the man they call "Smoke," but I do 100000% agree with him here. Take a look: One door closes and another opens! "I’ll be honest, I don’t even watch anymore," Stewart told the Oil and Whiskey podcast. "It is, it is so neutered. I mean, they’re driving cars with 500 horsepower. When I, at the peak when I was running, we were at 875 horsepower, those things. And then they cut the nuts off of them. We went down to a 775 horsepower package and I was miserable. I’m like, these things are pieces of s–t. "I’m going to do a commercial tomorrow with Dodge and Ram and we’re promoting a truck that has 777 horsepower that you can buy off a showroom floor. And you can go to Talladega to the truck race and outrun that thing by theory with more power from a street truck that you can buy. "It’s like, NASCAR, wake the f–k up. What are we doing?" Yeah, I mean — it's tough to argue with Tony Stewart on anything he just said. It's all true. It's all correct. The funny thing is, Tony is actually getting back in a car later this month! He's set to race the No. 25 Ram for Kaulig Racing in the Truck Series race at Talladega on Oct. 23. It's funny because Tony notoriously HATED restrictor plate race when he drove. HATED them. Mocked them all the time. And now he's gonna be back in a truck at 'Dega because he needs to promote Dodge. Everyone has a price! Speaking of drivers making stunning comebacks to the sport ... Where in the world did THIS come from? Dirty air, a dirty team & a really dirty (ALLEGED!) affair Per Jordan Bianchi of The Athletic, Kasey Kahne, now 46, is set to come out of retirement and drive a Spire truck full-time next season. Why? I have no earthly idea. None. Kahne hasn't raced since 2018, and he's only made six Truck Series starts over his career. For those who forget, the 31-time race winner retired at the end of that 2018 season due to health reasons, pointing towards dehydration as a big factor. As Bianchi noted, the Truck races are the shortest of all three, so it does make sense for Kahne to return to that specific series. Personally, I just hope we get more commercials like this next season with NASCAR's biggest heartthrob back behind the wheel: Man, we had it so good back then, and we just pissed it all away. Remember how great NASCAR commercials used to be? Heck, any commercial, for that matter. Now, they're all just Ozempic ads and Big Pharma crap. Disgusting. What a fall from grace. OK, let's quickly jam the pedal to the floor and rapid-fire through a couple quickies on the way out ... First? Here's how yesterday's race ended, which is extra special because you get to see Kyle Larson racing Kyle Busch's iconic No. 5 Kellogg's scheme from back in the day: See? Solid finish. Solid race! Could you make an actual pass? Not really. Dirty air still rules all, unfortunately. It's undefeated in this Next Gen car, and I fear it will always be. But it is what it is at this point. Not much you can do about this until the offseason: Ooooooooooof. Just a brutal clip. Don't let Tony see it! He'll freak out. Next? On the way out, let's go ahead and check in on Brad Keselowski, who is leaving his own RFK race team after this month: Pretty shocking news out of the NASCAR world late last week. Brad Keselowski came in to Roush-Fenway Racing five years ago and really, I thought, turned that place around. They were pretty irrelevant before Brad arrived, and this year they had two of the three cars in the Chase. Brad said his five-year contract expires this year, so that's part of the reason he's leaving. Obviously, there's a lot more meat on this bone, because the results have been good. I've seen some rumblings that the organization wanted him to transition into a more managerial role, while he preferred to keep racing. If that's the case, I'm with Brad. He's a NASCAR champ and a future Hall of Famer. If you wanna keep racing ... keep racing. Don't let anyone else tell you otherwise! OK, that's it for today. Solid week. A weird one, but a solid one. On the way out, here's NASCAR Truck Series driver Jennifer Jo Cobb owing the wife of spotter Clayton Hughes a whopping $850,000 after she won a civil court case in which she accused Cobb of seducing her husband before their ultimate divorce in 2021.
